oracle_provenance: Friis (1946) free-space transmission equation, standard textbook RF engineering; independently hand-verified before implementation. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded free-space RF link budget checking link closure above a declared receiver sensitivity; not a protocol certification or real-environment RF measurement.

cases.question: At 10 m with typical Bluetooth-class parameters, does the link close with positive margin above a -90 dBm sensitivity?
At a much longer distance, does the same link fail to close, correctly reflecting the model's own inverse-square-law behavior?
Must a non-positive distance be rejected rather than producing an undefined path loss?
Does doubling the distance increase free-space path loss by the model's own signature ~6.02 dB (20*log10(2)), discriminating genuine inverse-square-law behavior from an arbitrary result?
